title: Resolve one conflict between worthwhile goods

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A priority is a reason for this decision under these conditions, not a permanent ranking of people or goods. An exception should identify a relevant changed need rather than favor whoever benefits from it.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Lee has promised a 60-minute family visit on Saturday. An optional extra shift conflicts with it and pays 40 units. Essentials are covered this week;40 would increase a repair reserve, with no urgent repair. The relative welcomes asking about Sunday, but has not agreed. Lee values both reliability and financial security.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare keeping Saturday with asking to move the visit. State what must happen before either plan is settled, a reversal condition and the strongest cost of your preference.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: An optional event conflicts with an agreed care shift. The organizer says “your contribution matters.” Does that remove the care obligation?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Keeping Saturday protects an existing promise and forgoes 40. Asking about Sunday can be responsible if the shift is not accepted on assumed consent. Later fiction: Sunday is declined, so the original promise remains unless genuinely renegotiated. A newly essential uncovered expense could justify revisiting the balance, not silently erasing the promise. Partial: choose plausibly but omit the lost good. Incorrect: call the unconfirmed Sunday visit agreed.
criteria: Actual obligations and optional goods differ
Reversal conditions are relevant and reciprocal

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. The event’s good is real, but suitable accepted coverage or an appropriate renegotiation is needed before relying on release from care. Praise does not provide coverage.
